title: System Design Capstone: Building the Learning Platform
concept: Design a production system end to end and prove each decision with evidence: requirements with numbers, the simplest architecture and its source of truth, validation at the boundary, lost updates and optimistic concurrency, event-driven projections, caches that are not single points of failure, rebuilding derived state, per-user rate limits, backpressure, graceful degradation and an idempotent vertical slice, ending in an architecture review of a learning platform.
description: An expert capstone for engineers who design and own systems. You design the CodeDev learning platform itself - progress, submissions and the leaderboard - one decision at a time, and every decision is checked against evidence: a capacity estimate, a lost update between two browser tabs, a leaderboard that disappeared with its Redis node, a cache outage that took down the whole API, a submission spike that filled the queue, a duplicate event that counted a lesson twice. Each lesson turns a design choice into small, tested TypeScript components - a validating progress service, a leaderboard projection, a per-user rate limiter, a bounded queue that answers 429, fallbacks and an idempotent end-to-end slice - and the course ends with an Architecture Review Board on real evidence. 13 lessons with design-decision quizzes and TypeScript challenges graded with in-memory stores and fakes.

lessons.title: Requirements with numbers: users, load and what must never break
The simplest architecture that works, and its source of truth
Progress service: validate at the boundary, keep the rules in one place
Lost updates: two requests, one row, optimistic concurrency
Event-driven projections: a leaderboard from progress events
Caching without a single point of failure
Recovery: rebuilding derived state after the cache is lost
Backpressure: a bounded submission queue that answers 429
Graceful degradation: when an optional dependency fails
The vertical slice: API to leaderboard, idempotent end to end
Scaling & cost: what changes when traffic and the team grow
Architecture Review Board: defend the design with evidence
